messages:
maria-support: Hey team, ACME reported a big p99 spike starting ~2024-10-12 14:02 UTC after we rolled the continuous-batcher config change. Customer says many requests > 3s (used to be < 400ms). attaching short logs and an example request id: req_0a9f3b

aj-eng-sre: Thanks — can you paste the exact config change and the deploy id?

maria-support: Deploy ID: deploy-2024-10-12-03, change was: grace_window_ms: 8 -> 50, linger_ms: 5 -> 15, max_batch_tokens: 2048 -> 4096 (per-release note). Customer tenant: acme-corp-42.

liam-eng-platform: Noted. That increase in grace_window and batch size could amplify tail latency for tiny prompt traffic. Any p95/p99 timeseries?

maria-support: Short clip from metrics: p95 baseline 120ms -> 340ms, p99 baseline 380ms -> 2.9s. Spike correlates with a mini-burst at 14:01:30 UTC; throughput seemed normal. Attached request sample payload (very small prompt, 6 tokens).

aj-eng-sre: Can you repro locally with that tenant shaping? Steps we usually run: 1) set up a small client sending 30 rps of tiny requests 2) ensure continuous-batcher enabled with new values 3) record per-request latencies and batch sizes. If we see high p99 and batch sizes >1 with long wait, it matches hold-time amplification.

maria-support: I kicked off a repro harness (link: https://ci.internal/repro/6532). Initial run shows many requests waiting near the grace window boundary and then a long tokenization/kv-cache path once dispatched.

devops-bot: Deploy deploy-2024-10-12-03 was rolled out to 60% of hosts at 2024-10-12T03:00:00Z. Canary passed health checks.

liam-eng-platform: Two hypotheses: (A) larger max_batch_tokens increases batching packing time for mixed prompt lengths (small prompts waiting for a coalesced large slot), (B) grace_window increased means tiny bursts hold longer to try to fill batches -> higher tail when bursts end up with hit to kernel path. Both fit symptom.

nina-product: Customer impact: ACME's flows are mostly tiny completions (chat UI). They saw user-facing timeouts. We need a quick mitigation and a followup to better defaults per workload.

aj-eng-sre: Immediate mitigations to try (in order): 1) rollback grace_window to 8ms for tenant acme-corp-42 (per-tenant override) 2) set max_batch_tokens back to 2048 globally or per-tenant 3) enable tiny-prompt fastpath (force single-request dispatch if prompt tokens < 16) 4) add temporary routing to a low-latency pool. Which can we enact fast?

liam-eng-platform: We can do a per-tenant override using config service. Command: 
```
POST /api/v1/tenants/acme-corp-42/config
{
  "continuous_batcher": { "grace_window_ms": 8, "max_batch_tokens": 2048 }
}
```
I'll apply that to 2 regions (us-west-2/us-east-1) now, should take ~30s to propagate to routing layer.

maria-support: Please do. I'll notify the customer and ask them to watch UX.

kevin-cust-rep: ACME confirms they've seen improvement within 2 minutes after you applied the override — p99 back down to ~420ms. Thanks!

aj-eng-sre: Great. For a longer fix we should: - instrument batch-size distribution vs wait-time per tenant - introduce a tiny-prompt fastpath that bypasses coalesce logic - add configurable thresholds for switching to single-request mode when mean request tokens < X and instantaneous RPS < Y. Also consider adaptive grace_window that decays under bursty tiny traffic.

liam-eng-platform: I'll open a tracking ticket and a short experiment: start with tiny-prompt fastpath gate via runtime flag + metrics. If safe, we flip on for tenants with >70% small prompts.

nina-product: Add product acceptance criteria: no UX regressions, measurable reduction in p99 for small-prompt tenants, and no throughput loss for batchy customers.

aj-eng-sre: Repro notes for the run we saved: curl snippet below to reproduce the burst pattern used in CI (30 rps, 6 tokens, 12000 requests):
```
wrk -t4 -c30 -d30s --latency "http://internal-proxy/serve?model=redwood-small" --script=./scripts/tiny_prompt.lua
# tiny_prompt.lua sends prompt: "Q" repeated => ~6 tokens
```

maria-support: I'll attach the customer's logs and monitoring links to the ticket. Anything else before we close the escalation?

aj-eng-sre: Leave this open until we have the fastpath experiment running and a postmortem that documents default values and per-tenant overrides. Mark P1 until then.

maria-support: Ack, setting status P1 and adding notes. :white_check_mark: 

kevin-cust-rep: ACME sent a quick thank-you — they're monitoring. No immediate complaints.

liam-eng-platform: Created platform issue PF-8473: "tiny-prompt fastpath + adaptive grace window" with links to repro, metrics, and per-tenant override rollout steps. Assigning to aj-eng-sre and liam-eng-platform. ETA: experiment in 3 days.

nina-product: I'll schedule a short sync with ACME to review longer-term tuning and see if they want a dedicated low-latency pool.

aj-eng-sre: Thanks all. Closing slack thread when PF-8473 has initial experiment results.
